problem: While trying to repair replication an engineer removed data from the primary database server.
title: GitLab accidentally removes production data and publishes a candid postmortem
context: On 31 January 2017 replication between GitLab.com's primary and secondary database servers lagged and then failed.
decision_made: Restore from a six-hour-old backup, and publish live updates and a full postmortem openly.
action_taken: Service was restored after roughly 18 hours; Git repositories and wikis were unavailable but not affected by the data loss.
observed_outcome: About six hours of database data was lost, affecting an estimated 5,000 projects, 5,000 comments and 700 new user accounts.
lessons: Open, timely incident communication can preserve trust even when the incident is severe.
limitations: The claim that backups failed was not confirmed; the sources describe a replication failure and restoration from a six-hour-old backup. Trust effects were not measured.

claims.claim_text: GitLab published a postmortem attributing the outage to accidental removal of data from its primary database server.
The postmortem estimated about 5,000 projects, 5,000 comments and 700 new user accounts were affected.
